newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: South Africa's Mandela arrives in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Mandela arrives in Singapore.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela arrived in Singapore on Wednesday for a two-day visit as part of a four-nation Asian tour.
Mandela, accompanied by Graca Machel, the widow of former Mozambique president Samora Machel, was received at the airport by Singapore President Ong Teng Cheong.
He is accompanied by a 50-member delegation, including ministers, senior officials and businessmen.
Mandela, who has been to the Philippines and Brunei, will meet Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew, visit Singapore's massive port and attend a dinner hosted by Ong on Wednesday.
He is due to deliver a lecture on "South and Southern Africa into the next century" and attend a lunch hosted by Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong on Thursday before leaving for Malaysia.

Mandela has said he is keen to deepen economic ties with the seven-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and learn how to raise the living conditions of his own people from the region's economic success.
ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Goh is due to return to Singapore on Thursday morning after a 10-day tour of South Africa, Zimbabwe, Namibia and Botswana. Goh made a four-day stop in South Africa.

At a dinner hosted by Mandela during his visit, Goh said Singapore was ready to contribute to South Africa's nation-building efforts and to strengthen trade and investment ties between the two countries.
Total bilateral trade was Singapore $945 million (US$665.5 million) in 1996, with Singapore's exports to South Africa comprising just over 65 percent of the total.
